name: Ensemble accusation

intent.purpose: Establish the power imbalance and introduce the evidence.
intent.reason: The audience needs the geography of one standing against five seated before the accusation lands.
intent.attention: Mara's isolation, then Len's hand and the letter.
intent.relationships: The council is united and seated; Mara is alone and standing. Len acts as the council's accuser.

staging.positions: Council members are grouped along the table, with Mara at the open end and Len nearest to her.
staging.facing: The council faces toward Mara; Mara faces the table.
staging.eyelines: Most eyes are on Mara as Len places the letter.
staging.movement: Len reaches and sets the letter down, then sits back.
staging.camera: A wide, slightly elevated frame from the far side of the table with a slow, subtle push in.

editorial.cutOut: Cut to the letter and Len as he speaks, once the letter is down.
editorial.timing: Measured. Let the silence before the accusation register.

advanced.continuity: The letter stays sealed and remains in front of Mara for the rest of the scene.
advanced.assumptions: Camera position and table orientation are assumed.

shots.title: The Letter Is Placed
shots.sourceExcerpt:
## INT. COUNCIL ROOM - NIGHT

Five council members sit together. Mara stands alone at the open end of their table. Len places a sealed letter in front of her.
shots.description: Opening: a wide, slightly elevated frame of the night council room. Five council members sit together along the table, and Mara stands alone at its open end. Len reaches down the table and places a sealed letter in front of Mara, then withdraws his hand. The camera holds mostly still, with a slow, slight push in. Ending: still wide, the letter resting before Mara, Mara and the seated council facing each other across the empty length of the table.
shots.atmosphere: Night interior with low, formal light pooled over the table and darkness at the edges. Hushed, tense stillness.
shots.music: Near silence; at most a faint low sustained tone.

intent.purpose: Tie the evidence to Len's accusation.
intent.reason: Linking the object and the speaker in one take makes the letter the weight behind his words.
intent.attention: The seal first, then Len's face.
intent.relationships: Len presents the evidence as conclusive.

staging.positions: The letter is in the foreground; Len is seated behind it.
staging.eyelines: Len looks at Mara, slightly off-lens on her side.
staging.camera: A low table-level frame with a rack focus from the letter to Len.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from the wide on the completed placement of the letter. The close object frame is clearly distinct.
editorial.cutOut: Cut to Mara for her reply.

advanced.continuity: Len's eyeline matches Mara's position at the open end.
advanced.assumptions: Len's seat being nearest Mara is assumed.

shots.title: Your Seal
shots.description: Opening: a close, low angle on the sealed letter on the table, with Len soft in the background. Focus racks to Len, now framed in a medium close-up, as he delivers his line with flat certainty, looking toward Mara. Ending: a medium close-up on Len, the letter's edge soft in the foreground.
shots.atmosphere: Quiet and controlled; the room seems to hold its breath.

intent.purpose: Give Mara her denial and implied counter-accusation.
intent.reason: Her steadiness must be read in her face, at her own level.
intent.attention: Mara's eyes moving from the letter to Len.
intent.relationships: Mara does not plead. She returns the suspicion to the room.

staging.positions: Mara stands at the open end of the table.
staging.facing: She faces toward Len and the council.
staging.eyelines: She looks down to the letter, then up to Len, matching his eyeline.
staging.camera: A static camera at standing eye level, slightly lower than her eyes so she keeps her stature.

editorial.cutIn: Cut on Len's completed line to her answer.
editorial.cutOut: Cut to the youngest councillor's reaction after Mara's held look.
editorial.timing: Leave a beat after the line for the implication to land.

advanced.assumptions: The direction of her look toward Len is a staging assumption.

shots.title: Someone Has Learned Both
shots.sourceExcerpt:
### MARA

Then someone has learned both.
shots.description: Opening: a medium close-up on Mara, standing, the seated council soft and out of focus beyond her. She looks from the letter up to Len and answers evenly. She holds her gaze afterward. Ending: Mara in a steady medium close-up, unbowed.
shots.atmosphere: Still. Her composure cools the room.

intent.reason: This glance is the only sign of hesitation, so it needs isolation.
intent.attention: The movement of the eyes from Mara to Len.
intent.relationships: The youngest briefly questions Len rather than Mara.

staging.positions: The youngest councillor is seated at the table.
staging.movement: Eyes only, perhaps a slight turn of the head.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from Mara's held look to a listener reacting to her words.
editorial.cutOut: Cut wide as the council begins turning away.

advanced.continuity: The eyeline directions must match the positions of Mara and Len.
advanced.assumptions: The youngest's seat position is assumed.

shots.title: The Youngest Looks at Len
shots.sourceExcerpt: The youngest councillor looks at Len. One by one the others turn their chairs away from Mara. Mara stays standing.
shots.description: Opening: a close-up on the youngest councillor, seated among the others, eyes on Mara. Their eyes then move to Len and hold there. Ending: a close-up of the youngest councillor looking toward Len.
shots.music: None, or the faintest held note.

intent.purpose: Show the council's collective judgment and Mara's refusal to yield.
intent.reason: The rejection unfolds in sequence and needs to play in one uninterrupted frame from Mara's side.
intent.attention: Each chair turning in turn, with Mara's stillness constant in the foreground.
intent.relationships: The council closes ranks against Mara. She stays apart and unbowed.

staging.positions: Mara is in the foreground at the open end; the council is seated down the table.
staging.facing: The council turns from facing Mara to facing away.
staging.eyelines: Mara looks down the table at them.
staging.movement: The chairs turn one by one; Mara stays still.
staging.camera: A static wide frame, possibly with a very slow drift closer to Mara.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from the youngest councillor's close-up to the reverse wide as the turning begins. The difference in scale and angle avoids a jump.
editorial.cutOut: Ends the scene on Mara standing alone.
editorial.timing: Let each turn have its own beat, and hold at the end.

advanced.continuity: The letter remains on the table in front of Mara, and Mara never sits.
advanced.assumptions: The order of the turning chairs and Mara's exact placement are assumed.
advanced.longTakeIdea: Could be extended manually to hold longer on Mara after the last chair turns, within the clip maximum.

shots.title: The Council Turns Away
shots.sourceExcerpt: The youngest councillor looks at Len. One by one the others turn their chairs away from Mara. Mara stays standing.
shots.description: Opening: a wide frame from behind and beside Mara at the open end of the table, her shoulder in the foreground and the whole seated council facing her down the length of the table, the letter before her. One by one, the council members turn their chairs away from Mara. Mara stays standing and does not move. Ending: Mara upright in the foreground, facing a table of turned backs.
shots.atmosphere: Chairs scrape one after another in the silence, a slow ritual of rejection.
shots.music: A low, restrained tone may rise beneath the final turns, or silence holds.

strategies.dramaticProgression: An accusation lands through evidence (the letter). Len names it as Mara's. Mara offers a denial that is also a counter-accusation. The youngest councillor's glance at Len briefly leaves the question open. Then the council collectively rejects Mara, and she refuses to yield.
strategies.visualProgression: The scene opens on a geography of separation: five seated councillors against one standing figure. It tightens into the exchange over the letter. A single reaction close-up briefly breaks the council's unity. It ends wide from Mara's end of the table as the council physically turns its backs, leaving Mara isolated but upright.
strategies.audienceInformation: The audience does not learn who wrote the letter. Len's certainty and Mara's composed reply both remain plausible. The youngest councillor's look at Len plants a doubt without confirming it.
strategies.spatialAnchors: A long table with five seated council members. One end is open, and Mara stands there alone. The sealed letter sits on the table in front of Mara, and Len is within reach of it. All placements are staging assumptions until reference-supported.
